correctness.rationale: The proof has two necessary conditions and a direct converse. The last 0-block forces at least k selections from the final 1-block. Any kTDS has at least k+1 vertices because selected vertices require k distinct selected neighbors. Conversely the final 1-block is universal and every earlier vertex is adjacent to all of it, so those two inequalities satisfy every open-neighborhood constraint. Binomial counting then gives the polynomial, and every larger feasible set contains a feasible size-(k+1) subset. The packaged verifier exhaustively confirms the characterization, coefficients, and inclusion-minimality for all 511 connected threshold creation strings through order 10.

originality.rationale: The claim is an all-cardinality, all-k structural theorem for connected threshold graphs. The closest parameter-specific source develops general kTDS theory and complete-multipartite formulas; the closest threshold-specific source gives optimization algorithms for total vector domination; the closest ordinary-total source gives total-domishold separation. None of the inspected statements covers or implies the two-condition feasible-family classification, the polynomial, or the two-parameter profile collapse.

value.rationale: The result upgrades optimization-only threshold coverage to a complete feasible-family description simultaneously for every multiplicity k. It determines every coefficient, all inclusion-minimal solutions, and an exact invariance showing that the full sequence of enumerators forgets all creation-block data except order and final-block size. This is a natural structural question attached directly to an established domination parameter, not an arbitrary finite slice.
